title: Godement augmentation computes sections on principal affine intersections
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$ satisfy $\operatorname{span}(f)=I$. On $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$ take the specified Godement augmentation $e:\mathcal O_U[0]\to G_U$ of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-godement-construction]. For every $p\geq0$ and increasing tuple $t:\operatorname{Fin}(p+1)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, evaluation of $e$ on $V_t=\bigcap_j(U\cap D(f_{t(j)}))$, with the family of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-ordered-cech-construction], is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal O_U(V_t)$-modules. This asserts a property of the specified augmentation, not the existence of some resolution.

proof.text: In principalIntersection_affine, take W to be the finite nonempty intersection of the ambient basic opens D(f(t j)). Mathlib IsAffineOpen.Spec_basicOpen and IsAffineOpen.iInf show W is affine. Since f(t 0) belongs to span(range f)=I, W lies in the ideal complement. IsAffineOpen.preimage_of_isOpenImmersion then proves its inverse image under the open inclusion is affine; extensionality identifies this inverse image with the specified alternatingCechIntersection. This includes empty intersections and zero rings; an empty generating list has no increasing tuples.

For any affine open V of any scheme X, use the abelian-group-valued RingedSpace.openModuleSections X V. The structure module is quasi-coherent by SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_unit, so affine vanishing makes it right-acyclic. Its single complex has right-acyclic terms by transport along singleObjXSelf in degree zero and by the zero-object property in other degrees.

The choose_spec of the existing specified Godement construction supplies ModuleCupGodementModel for exactly ringComplexGodementUnit. Hence moduleCup_godement_model_quasiIso makes that augmentation a quasi-isomorphism. The same model identifies its natural-degree terms with godementObject applied to the preceding iterate, so they are flasque. For open sections, Scheme.Modules.rightAcyclic_of_isFlasque applies the source dimension-shifting criterion: injectives are flasque, the flasque quotient and section-surjectivity facts give its hypotheses. This proves right-acyclicity on V directly, without restriction of sheaves. HomologicalComplex.prop_extend_X supplies the zero negative terms.

Enough injectives is supplied by moduleSheaves_abelian_enoughInjectives. Both complexes vanish below zero. Apply Functor.quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic to the actual augmentation with bound zero and the two termwise right-acyclicity proofs. Its conclusion is the desired quasi-isomorphism after forgetting O_X(V)-module structure. The exact faithful forgetful functor ModuleCat O_X(V) to AddCommGrpCat reflects quasi-isomorphisms by HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_iff_of_preservesHomology; the iterated evaluation agrees definitionally with openModuleSections. Apply this affine-open result to principalIntersection_affine.

lean.statement:
theorem ringComplexGodement_affineSections (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (I : Ideal A)
    (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) (t : Fin (p + 1) ↪o Fin r),
      QuasiIso (((SheafOfModules.forget.{u}
        (moduleRings (ringComplexOpen A I).toScheme.toRingedSpace) ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation.{u}
          (moduleRings (ringComplexOpen A I).toScheme.toRingedSpace).obj
          (op (alternatingCechIntersection
            (ringComplexPrincipalCover A I f) t))).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
              (ringComplexGodementUnit (ringComplexOpen A I).toScheme))
